Hi Alex / Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + the follow-up items we discussed around tool/function-calling integration patterns and how Redwood would typically approach these for FinApps. High level notes below, then clear next steps.

What we heard as success criteria:
- Low-latency, reliable orchestration of model requests + external tools for real-time UX (sub-200ms where possible for core paths).
- Clear, auditable semantics for tool calls (schemas, retries, idempotency), especially for actions that change state.
- Fast and accurate retrieval/semantic search for banking docs (embeddings + reranker pipeline).

Technical areas we covered + recommendations:
1) SDK setup & auth
   - Recommend starting with our Node/Python SDK for quick PoC; uses API keys for hosted and mTLS for private deployments.
   - Auth details: API key short-lived tokens + optional request-scoped idempotency keys for write tools.

2) Routing & model variants
   - Route by policy: latency-sensitive routes map to smaller low-latency model variants; quality routes to larger models or semantic rerankers.

3) Structured output & tool calling
   - Use explicit tool definitions (tool_name, input_schema, output_schema, error_contract).
   - Prefer deterministic validators on outputs; fall back to verifier tool for ambiguous outputs.

4) Embeddings & rerankers
   - Store vectors in your existing vector store (we support Pinecone/Weaviate/managed options).
   - Index update cadence depends on doc churn — starting point: nightly refresh + realtime for critical docs.

Tool/function-calling integration patterns (short)
- Synchronous single-tool calls for read-only lookups (e.g. account lookup).
- Async fan-out for long-running tools (e.g. ledger reconciliation) with callback/webhook to update state.
- Parallel tools (scatter-gather): run search + external scoring in parallel, then aggregate via a lightweight combiner model.
- Error handling: classify errors (retryable, non-retryable); use exponential backoff and fallbacks to safe defaults.

Hi Alex / Sara —

Quick dive on your questions and an example pattern we recommend. See attached redwood_tool_definitions_example.json for a canonical tool schema. High-level guidance below.

Partial failures (parallel tools)
- Pattern: scatter-gather with a lightweight combiner. Combiner should be tolerant of missing tool outputs and use feature-availability flags.
- Behavior choices:
  - Best-effort aggregation: continue with partial results and surface confidence scores to the client;
  - Failover: if a critical tool fails (as defined in tool metadata), fallback to a trusted single-source scorer.
- Implementation tip: mark tools with "critical": true/false in the tool definition file and enforce in orchestrator.

Retry & idempotency
- Tool definition fields we use: retry_policy { max_attempts, backoff_ms, retry_on: [timeout, 5xx] }, idempotency_key_fields: []
- For side-effecting tools (payments, record writes) require idempotency_key and only allow once semantically; record responses in a durable store.

Tool definitions (example fields) — see attached but inline example below:
- tool_name: "customer_lookup"
- input_schema: {"account_id":"string"}
- output_schema: {"customer_name":"string","status":"string"}
- sync: true/false
- critical: true/false
- retry_policy: { max_attempts:3, backoff_ms:200 }
- idempotency_key_fields: ["request_id"]

Parallel / async patterns
- For long-running tools: schedule background tasks and return an operation_id to the client. Use webhook callbacks or polling endpoints.
- For low-latency UX: keep synchronous paths to strictly read-only or pre-warmed cached results.

Structured output validation
- We recommend server-side validators that reject/flag outputs that don't match output_schema. For borderline cases run an automatic verification tool (fallback model) that checks intent and entity extraction.

Embeddings / reranker cadence
- Hybrid strategy: nightly bulk refresh + per-event incremental upserts for hot docs. Use TTL on vectors for documents that change frequently and keep an audit log of vector updates.

Attached: redwood_tool_definitions_example.json (tool schema + sample tool entries)
